author: brahma_4u
author_bio: Building Energy Superintelligence at @energyailabs | EV DOCTOR™
text:
The biggest electricity blackout in history wasn't an efficiency problem.

July 2012. 
Roughly 620 million Indians in the dark. The enquiry committee found states drawing more than their schedule, and state control rooms not responding enough to instructions to cut back. 

The warnings went out. People didn't act in time.

Now look at what we're plugging into that grid. 

PM Surya Ghar crossed 50 lakh rooftop solar homes in about two years; the whole decade before it added 7.9 lakh. Each one is a small power plant nobody dispatches. 

Yet the grid still plans in 96 fifteen-minute blocks a day, and the real-time market takes about 75 minutes from schedule revision to delivery. A single cloud can swing a solar plant's output in under a minute.

This is why I think energy needs superintelligence, and efficiency is the least interesting reason. 

You can't hire enough engineers to coordinate 50 lakh rooftops. 

More staff won't fix AT&C losses still near 15%, which means about one unit in seven a DISCOM buys leaks, gets stolen, or never turns into a paid bill. 

Even CERC's plan to cut that 75 minutes to 50 assumes the bidding is automated.

Efficiency saves a few percent. Autonomy decides whether the lights stay on.

text:
Respected Rekha Gupta ji,
@gupta_rekha
I have been closely watching the administration in Delhi over the past several months. Beyond campaign promises several initiatives now visible on the ground deserve attention. Leaving aside Yamuna cleaning and the schemes already widely discussed a number of other programmes appear to be making a practical difference in people’s lives. The first is the DURGA scheme for women and transgender persons. After Cabinet approval, 1,300 pink electric autos are to be allotted in the first phase 1,170 for women and 130 for transgender beneficiaries.  Ownership and self-employment come together with safer last-mile travel. This is not merely a vehicle scheme; it is a route to dignified livelihood. The second is the Delhi Lakshmi Yojana. Eligible women aged 21 to 60, within the prescribed family-income limit, are to receive ₹2,500 every month. The registration portal has been opened, with the aim of reaching lakhs of women through direct financial support. Relief of this kind should show in household expenses, not only on paper. The third is the electrification of public transport. Delhi now has the country’s largest electric bus fleet, with more than 5,000 e-buses on the roads. Recently, 50 new electric buses were flagged off, a Delhi–Rewari interstate e-bus service was launched, and ladies-special e-bus services were expanded. The new EV policy also adds charging infrastructure and incentives for two-wheelers and commercial vehicles. This is one of the more practical ways to cut vehicular pollution. The fourth is the transformation of a garbage mountain. About 70 lakh metric tonnes of legacy waste have been removed from the Okhla landfill. An Oxygen Park of around 37 acres is planned on the reclaimed land. An area long associated with stench and dust is being turned into a space for greenery and cleaner air. The fifth is the Delhi portal for the PM Surya Ghar scheme. For rooftop solar systems of up to 3 kW, the Centre and the Delhi government together offer subsidy so that eligible households can install panels without a heavy upfront cost. Lower electricity bills and possible income from the rooftop make this a green scheme that can reach ordinary homes. Whether Delhi’s residents have spoken of these efforts enough or not, I am impressed by the direction of the work. A woman who wants to see her country improve finds genuine reassurance in such concrete steps.
With regards.

text:
Rooftop Solar: The Zero-Bill Myth That’s Costing Indians Real Money (And the Smarter Way to Think About It)

Most Indians installing rooftop solar today do so with one big dream: zero electricity bills forever.

You’ve seen the ads. You’ve heard the promises under PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana. “Free power for 300 units.” “Say goodbye to discom bills.” It sounds like magic.

But here’s the uncomfortable truth nobody wants to say out loud:

Rooftop solar almost never gives you a literal ₹0 bill.  
And chasing that myth could lead you to wrong sizing, wrong expectations, and disappointing returns.

I dug deep into real installations, net-metering rules across states, and actual consumer bills. Here’s what actually happens.

### The Real Math (Not the Marketing Version)

1. Energy charges? Yes, those can drop to near zero.  
   Net metering credits your daytime solar generation against your consumption. If your system is sized right and you consume most power during the day, your variable energy cost can vanish.

2. But fixed charges, demand charges, and meter rent? They stay.  
   Every state electricity board charges you based on your sanctioned load (kW), not just what you consume. These are non-negotiable even if you generate 100% of your daytime power. Many households still see ₹200–800/month in fixed components.

3. Night-time usage kills the “zero” dream.  
   Solar doesn’t produce after sunset. If your ACs, refrigerators, or EV chargers run at night, you’re pulling from the grid. No battery? You pay full tariff for those units.

4. Billing cycles and seasonal variations matter.  
   Monsoon months = lower generation. Summer peak = higher consumption. Even perfectly sized systems often show small bills 3–4 months a year.

Real-world example: A 5 kW system in a typical Delhi NCR home producing ~600–650 units/month might reduce the bill from ₹8,000 to ₹400–900. Not zero. But still life-changing.

### Why the “Zero Bill” Myth Persists

- Influencers and some vendors simplify the pitch for clicks.  
- Government schemes focus on “free electricity up to 300 units” – which is fantastic, but not the same as “zero bill.”  
- Early adopters with perfect daytime consumption patterns do hit zero some months – and everyone remembers those screenshots.

### The Smarter Question to Ask

Stop asking: “Will I get zero bill?”  
Start asking: “What’s my real payback period and lifetime savings?”

With current subsidies (up to ₹78,000 under PM Surya Ghar), falling panel prices, and 25-year system life, a well-designed rooftop solar plant still delivers:

- 70–90% reduction in total electricity cost  
- Payback in 4–6 years  
- Internal Rate of Return (IRR) of 18–25% (better than most fixed deposits or mutual funds)  
- Protection against 4–8% annual tariff hikes

That’s real wealth creation.

### How to Actually Maximize Savings (Practical Checklist)

- Size your system based on annual consumption, not just “300 units free.”  
- Prioritize daytime-heavy appliances (shift loads where possible).  
- Consider a small battery only if night usage is very high (currently expensive but prices are falling).  
- Choose a reputed installer who explains fixed charges transparently (avoid the ones promising “guaranteed zero bill”).  
- Track your first 12 months of bills religiously.

Rooftop solar isn’t broken.  
The marketing is.

It remains one of the best financial + environmental decisions a middle-class Indian household can make in 2026. Just go in with eyes wide open.

The sun is free.  
The bill will never be perfectly zero.  
But the savings? They’re very, very real.

Have you installed solar yet?  
Drop your actual bill reduction story below — the good, the bad, and the fixed-charge reality. Let’s kill the myth with real numbers.  

#RooftopSolar #PMSuryaGhar #SmartSavings #EnergyIndependence #IndiaGoesSolar

text:
To
Shri @narendramodi ji @PMOIndia
Hon’ble Prime Minister of India
South Block, Raisina Hill
New Delhi – 110011

*Subject: Suggestions for making @PMSuryaGhar financially viable and rapidly scalable for all Communities* 
Respected Pradhan Mantri ji, 
On behalf of the *Unity of Nations Action for Climate Change Council* (UNAccc), I wish to commend the Government of India for the visionary “PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana,” which has the potential to transform household energy access, reduce carbon emissions, and strengthen energy security.However, early ground‑level feedback from beneficiaries, vendors, and financial institutions indicates that current benchmark costs and implementation structures are making the scheme less attractive, especially for BPL and lower‑middle‑income households. We humbly submit the following findings and suggestions for your kind consideration.
 Realistic system cost for 3 kW rooftop solar 
Our technical and market assessment, based on direct B2B pricing from leading Gujarat/Maharashtra / NCR manufacturers (such as Waaree / Adani, Reliance and others), shows that actual costs for quality systems are significantly lower than many existing benchmark assumptions when middleman margins are removed.Illustrative calculation (current bulk direct‑from‑manufacturer rates):
Solar modules (Tier‑1 quality):
Average [₹7,500] per kW (range [₹6{,}000–9{,}000] per kW).
For 3 kW: approx. [₹22, 500].Inverter, DC/AC wiring, protection devices, earthing, MC4 connectors and balance of system: approx. [₹10, 000] for 3 kW.Module mounting structure (steel mounting suitable for typical RCC roofs): approx. [₹7,500] for 3 https://t.co/PEogP37voj realistic system cost for 3 kW rooftop plant (excl. unusual civil work):
Around ₹40,000 https://t.co/IfzxsRuWLz this cost level, a 3 kW system becomes genuinely affordable for BPL and economically weaker households, especially when combined with central subsidy and state‑level convergence.
" Impact on payback period and scheme attractiveness With system cost contained near ₹40,000 for 3 kW and generation of roughly 360–420 units per month (depending on site), the effective payback period for households can fall to around 2–3 years, compared to the 5–7 years often observed under current pricing structures.Such rapid payback:
Increases household willingness to participate without hesitation.Lowers NPA risk for banks and NBFCs financing small rooftop systems.
Directly supports your vision of “Muft Bijli” while minimising subsidy burden per unit of energy produced.This pricing also aligns with the bulk B2B rates currently available from Gujarat manufacturers, which UNAccc is already leveraging for climate‑action projects, resulting in faster ROI and higher deployment volumes.3. Key reasons for current cost inflation and slower Rollout from our field interactions, we observe the following cost‑escalating factors:Multiple layers of intermediaries (distributors, sub‑distributors, local vendors) adding 40–55% over direct manufacturer prices. Non‑standardised BoQ and over‑specification of certain components by some installers.Delayed and complex disbursement of subsidies, increasing working‑capital interest costs. Limited aggregation of demand at ward/block level, preventing true volume discounts.

These factors collectively weaken the economics for both consumers and EPC companies, slowing your flagship scheme.4. Suggestions for a faster, more efficient implementation Model to unlock the full potential of PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, we respectfully propose:
Direct manufacturer empanelment and bulk procurement Empanel reputable domestic manufacturers at national or state level.Allow DISCOMs/ULBs/State Nodal Agencies to procure panels and inverters directly at bulk rates, then allocate to empanelled local Mfg Co.s, @NitinNabin @rashtrapatibhvn

text:
Powering the Lanes. Harnessing the Skies

At BSES, we believe the future of power must work for the city as it is—crowded in some places and full of possibilities everywhere.

With this in mind, and aligned with the Delhi Government’s vision of a Viksit Delhi, BSES Yamuna Power Limited (BYPL) unveiled two initiatives: BSES’s first-of-its-kind 2 × 1,000 kVA smart pad-mounted substation at Amar Mohalla, Gandhi Nagar, and ‘Solarize East’, a community-driven rooftop solar programme.

Shri Harsh Malhotra, Hon’ble Union Minister of State for Road Transport & Highways and Corporate Affairs, and Shri Ashish Sood, Hon’ble Power Minister, Government of NCT of Delhi, inaugurated the substation and launched ‘Solarize East’.

‘Solarize East’ will make rooftop solar simpler for families—helping them understand the process, access benefits under the PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana and the Delhi Solar Policy, and move confidently from enquiry to installation. At the same time, the compact pad-mounted substation will make the local electricity network more reliable while adding capacity to meet the growing energy needs of congested areas.

Joining them on the occasion were Hon’ble MLAs Shri O. P. Sharma, Shri Abhay Verma, Shri Sanjay Goyal, Shri Ravi Negi and Dr Anil Goyal; Deputy Mayor Dr Monika Pant; and District Magistrate (East) Shri Vadodaria Karanjeet.

Representing the BSES leadership were Shri Amal Sinha, Director and Group CEO; Shri Abhishek Ranjan, CEO, BRPL; and Shri Santosh Kumar, COO, BYPL.

One initiative makes the most of limited space. The other unlocks the possibilities above our rooftops. Together, they bring East Delhi closer to a smarter, greener energy future.

text: #WATCH | Delhi CM Rekha Gupta says, "The ‘PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana’, introduced by the Prime Minister, is performing remarkably well across the country. We observed that the scheme was not gaining sufficient momentum in Delhi. We understood the challenges involved and found solutions. In today’s Cabinet meeting, a historic decision was taken to enable Delhi to take a decisive step towards solar energy. This initiative is driven by the vision of a ‘Developed India’ and a ‘Developed Delhi’, recognizing that the path to a developed India undoubtedly runs through a developed Delhi. Therefore, this decision is highly significant. Today, we have launched the next version of the Delhi Solar Energy Policy. Under this, households consuming up to 400 units of electricity will receive a 3 kW rooftop solar system at zero upfront cost, fully installed by the government without charging the consumer anything. This is a historic move. We have set a target to install these rooftop solar plants completely free of cost for 230,000 households...Our target is to install these solar systems on the rooftops of 230,000 households by March 2027. Existing electricity subsidies will continue, allowing households to enjoy both the subsidy benefits and the savings generated by solar power."

author: mnreindia
author_name: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE)
author_bio:
Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) 
Government of India
text:
On #CivilServicesDay 2026 MNRE organised a Breakaway Session on “Accelerating India’s Net-Zero Path through PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana” at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi. The session was chaired by Shri Santosh Sarangi, Secretary, MNRE, who highlighted India’s record addition of 51 GW renewable energy capacity in FY 2025-26, including 16.3 GW through Distributed Renewable Energy (DRE) under flagship schemes such as PM Surya Ghar and PM-KUSUM.
A context-setting presentation was delivered by Shri J.V.N. Subramanyam, Joint Secretary, MNRE, highlighting the strong progress under PM Surya Ghar with 56 lakh applications, 35 lakh households benefitted, and ₹19,500 crore subsidy transferred directly to citizens’ bank accounts.
The session featured valuable insights from esteemed panelists: Shri Narendra Bhooshan, Secretary, DoLR shared his experience from the State of Uttar Pradesh where rapid scale-up of RTS installations happened through strong monitoring and vendor ecosystem development; Shri Lokesh Chandra, ACS, Maharashtra and MD MSEDCL  highlighted Maharashtra’s success in solarising agricultural demand and reducing subsidy burden on the ex-chequer and reduction in electricity tariff; Shri Puneet Kumar, ACS, Energy Keralam informed  about Kerala’s pace of installations and future focus on BESS for rooftop solar and DRE for EV charging infrastructure; Dr. K.K. Dwivedi, ACS to CM and Power presented Assam’s rapid progress in RTS installations and future plans for pumped storage and battery energy systems; and Shri Abhishek Ranjan highlighted the advantages of installing BESS including alongwith RTS apart from urban clean energy innovation through net metering reforms. 

The deliberations reaffirmed that PM Surya Ghar is a transformative citizen-centric initiative advancing India’s energy transition journey by enabling households to directly participate in the clean energy transition.

#MNRE #PMSG #SolarEnergy

author_bio: 'INVEST UP', Lucknow, U.P., India, is the newly created Investment Promotion & Facilitation Agency of Government of Uttar Pradesh
text:
Uttar Pradesh delivered an outstanding performance at the PM Surya Ghar: Free Electricity Scheme Awards Ceremony held in New Delhi, securing top national rankings across multiple categories. The state ranked first in the high consumer base category for the highest number of consumer applications (102,035), solar installations (64,734) and vendor registrations (779). Lucknow also emerged as the country’s top-performing district in rooftop solar installations. With more than 5.64 lakh rooftop solar systems installed under the scheme, Uttar Pradesh continues to strengthen its leadership in clean energy adoption, energy self-reliance and sustainable development.

For more details, read the attached news article.
